newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet to debate Handlowy sale soon.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet to debate Handlowy sale soon.

text.p: The Polish government will soon discuss the privatisation of large state-owned Bank Handlowy SA, possibly already at its meeting next week, a deputy finance minister said on Wednesday.
"The government will soon discuss the privatisation plan of Bank Handlowy...possibly at its next meeting," Halina Wasilewska-Trenkner told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

Earlier in the day another deputy finance minister, Ryszard Pazura, told Reuters that Handlowy's privatisation next year could see equal 30-percent stakes offered to strategic investors and floated on the Warsaw bourse.

"The assumptions of the programme are 30 percent for a group of stable investors, 30 percent on the Warsaw bourse, 30 percent for future pension funds, five (percent) for employees, five (percent) for reprivatisation claims," Pazura said.
But he added that the plan submitted by Handlowy's management could still be changed when a firm chosen to advise on the privatisation provides a detailed plan.
The ministry has said a tender for a privatisation adviser would be announced by the end of the year.
Pazura said the budget could gain around 900 million zlotys in the sale.
Handlowy netted 390.3 million zlotys in this year's first half with a balance sheet total of 10.46 billion zlotys.

Pazura also said a public offering was envisioned next year for Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) but it would be preceded by a sale of a 65-percent stake to foreign and domestic institutional investors.
He said that by the end of the week an official advising contract for PBK's privatisation would be signed with HSBC Ivestment Services.
PBK netted 185.17 million zlotys over the first three quarters this year against 121.07 million zlotys for all of last year.
It had a balance sheet total of 8.37 billion zlotys after three quarters against 7.37 million zlotys at the end of 1995.
